四级汇总词汇 · 09英文原文

A Shift Someone Could Keep

能一直干下去的那班工 · 650 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A factory wanted to hire a new workforce after a senior mechanic announced his retirement. Its manager offered a steady wage, but the contract demanded an overnight shift without a fixed end. Several trainees applied and then withdrew. One needed sick leave for a disability. Another had a child at home. Inez, the union coordinator, asked why the company was struggling with employment while a dozen trained people were willing to work. She suspected the hours had made an otherwise decent job impossible to keep.

2An excessive workload made flexibility necessary, the manager said. Labor shortages could intensify after a breakdown. Inez asked to see weekly records before the union sought compensatory pay. The supervisor brought a bill and a list of hourly payments. Periodic faults in one workshop caused most of the late shifts. A nationwide staffing shortage had not caused those delays. The plant could resolve them internally with a disciplined crew, a spare tool, and an assurance that a second team would take over.

3The union proposed a voluntary late crew with additional pay. A clerk said seniority might exclude new migrant workers. Inez made equal access a priority. A consultant described the minimum regulatory protection and checked compliance. The plant could also compensate workers for a change at short notice. A supervisor wanted to opt for the simplest rotation. Inez asked him to consider which arrangement a worker with family duties would deem acceptable, and which would create avoidable hardship.

4The manager wanted a conditional clause allowing suspension of pay for absence. Inez distinguished intentional refusal from sick leave. An appeal could check an arbitrary penalty. Both sides accepted a disciplinary process and a prohibition on extending a shift without approval. They agreed that a worker who reported an urgent fault should not be penalized for a delay. The new accord still allowed a second crew to deal with a serious breakdown.

5The first week brought a test. A part failed after the early crew left. A trained worker was willing to help, but the spare cabinet was locked. The supervisor wanted to complain about the late team's progress. Instead, Inez asked him to identify the pressing obstacle. They found that a trainee had never been given a key. An orderly handover would eliminate most of the wait. They added the key to the shift list and arranged for a senior mechanic to demonstrate the repair before he retired.

6A secretary asked what to do in the meantime if a supervisor was involved in a complaint. The agreement gave an experienced colleague permission to act as a temporary coordinator. It would maintain essential coverage while a worker waited for an answer. A labor association said the change was encouraging. Staff still needed assurance that minimal compliance would not become the managerial aim. Inez recorded whether the new rule improved satisfaction from the worker's standpoint.

7A month later the schedule was still demanding but satisfactory. Fewer workers were dissatisfied. One vacancy had been advertised as full-time, although the workshop could employ another person part-time. The manager changed the status of that job and agreed to provide a demonstration for each trainee. That step accomplished more than a lengthy interview about confidence. A candidate who had withdrawn applied again. She had been accustomed to shared shifts elsewhere and knew which practical adjustment would make the offer useful.

8The retiring mechanic handed the trainee his key. A review found that the change met basic rules. It would still need to comply with federal rules and ensure that compensation was paid on time. One active union member asked whether it should initiate a winter review. Inez agreed to track any layoff and see whether overtime would exceed its new limit. The trainee looked at the clock. A colleague had arrived to relieve her. She could finish her shift without relying on a promise the factory had no way to keep.

四级汇总词汇 · 09中文译文

能一直干下去的那班工

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一位资深机修工宣布退休，工厂想招一批新人。经理开出的工资稳定，可合同要求上夜班，还没有固定结束时间。几名学员报了名又退出。一人因为身体障碍需要病假，另一人家里有孩子。工会协调员伊内丝问，明明有十多个受过培训的人愿意来，工厂为什么还是招不到人。她怀疑工作本身挺好，只是时间安排让人干不下去。

2经理说，活太多，工时得灵活。机器一坏，用工紧张还会加重。工会正式要求补偿前，伊内丝先看了每周记录。主管拿来一张账单和按小时支付的清单。多数晚班是一个车间反复故障造成的，与全国性的用工短缺无关。车间内部只要有守纪律的小队、一件备用工具和另一班能接手的保证，就能解决大部分问题。

3工会提议自愿上晚班，另发补贴。文员提醒，按资历排班可能把新来的外地工人排除在外。伊内丝优先考虑公平。顾问说明了最低监管要求，并检查他们是否遵守。临时改班也可以给工人补偿。主管倾向最简单的轮班法，伊内丝请他想一想，有家庭责任的工人能接受哪种安排，哪种又会给人平添困难。

4经理想加个条件，缺勤就暂停发薪。伊内丝把故意拒绝到岗和请病假分开，还提出用申诉约束随意处罚。双方接受纪律程序，禁止未经批准延长班次。工人及时报告紧急故障，不能因随后发生的耽误而受罚。按新协议，严重故障仍可请第二班处理。

5第一周就遇到了考验。早班走后一个零件坏了，有受过训练的工人愿意帮忙，备用柜却上着锁。主管想抱怨晚班干得慢。伊内丝请他先找最急的障碍。他们发现，学员从未领过钥匙。交班有条理些，大半等待就能省下。于是他们把钥匙写进交接清单，请老机修工退休前示范维修。

6一名秘书问，如果投诉恰好涉及主管，中间该怎么办。协议允许有经验的同事临时协调，等工人收到答复时，必要岗位仍有人。一个劳工组织觉得这个变化令人鼓舞。职工仍希望确认，管理的目标不会只剩达到最低要求。伊内丝从工人的角度记录，新规有没有让大家更满意。

7一个月后，工作依然累，但安排能接受，不满意的人少了。一个空缺原先写全职，车间其实可以再雇一名兼职。经理改了岗位性质，同意给每个新人做一次示范。这比面试时长篇谈自信更管用。一名撤回申请的人又报了名。她以前习惯和别人轮班，知道哪一项实际调整能让这份工作适合自己。

8即将退休的机修工把钥匙交给学员。复核认为，新安排达到了基本要求。工厂仍得遵守联邦规定，准时付补偿。一名活跃的工会会员问冬天是否要再查一次。伊内丝同意追踪裁员情况，并看加班有没有超出新上限。学员看了一眼钟。接班同事已经来了，她可以按时结束班次。
